course_arc: The arc runs from what a learner may lack, through the geometry, to the field equations and then outward to their consequences. Tier 1, prerequisites (1-3): mathematical-methods supplies linear algebra, calculus, differential equations and statistics; mechanics-and-newtonian-gravity supplies units, Lagrangian mechanics, Kepler orbits and Newtonian gravity as a field ending at Poisson's equation, which is the target GR must reproduce; electromagnetism-thermal-quantum supplies Maxwell theory as the template field theory plus the thermal and quantum facts later chapters lean on. A learner who already has these can test out and start at 4. Tier 2, flat spacetime (4-6): special-relativity rebuilds space and time geometrically and gives four-momentum; tensor-algebra turns the dot product into a machine and introduces one-forms and index grammar in inertial coordinates; matter-and-stress-energy uses both to show that energy, momentum, pressure and stress form one tensor, which is why all of it must gravitate. Tier 3, gravity becomes geometry (7-12): equivalence-principle argues from free fall and tides that gravity is spacetime structure and fixes the principles and Newtonian limit of motion; manifolds-and-metrics gives the mathematical stage; connection-and-parallel-transport teaches differentiation with changing bases (rehearsed in flat polar coordinates); geodesics-and-symmetries turns the connection into free-fall motion and adds Killing symmetries and conserved quantities; curvature measures failure of flatness and reads the Riemann tensor as tides; differential-forms-and-frames revisits the same geometry index-free and with orthonormal frames, supplying Cartan's efficient curvature method. Forms can be deferred by learners on a fast track; later domains cite them only for optional routes. Tier 4, the theory (13-14): einstein-field-equations combines curvature with stress-energy under the equivalence principle and studies the equations' structure, mass, and initial-value formulation; action-principles-and-field-theory re-derives them from an action and places GR beside gauge field theories. Tier 5, consequences and solutions (15-24) branch from tier 4 and can be taken in different orders. The spherical strand runs schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars, then orbits-light-and-tests (the classical and precision tests), then black-holes, then causal-structure-and-singularities, which abstracts the global tools first met at horizons. The radiation strand runs gravitational-waves (linearized theory and generation), then gravitational-wave-astronomy (detectors, data and sources, which also needs the stars and black holes strand). The cosmology strand runs cosmological-kinematics (geometry and measurement), cosmological-dynamics (Friedmann equations and models) and physical-cosmology (the observed universe and inflation); it needs only tiers 1-4 plus the causal-structure language for horizons and conformal diagrams. The arc closes at the frontier with quantum-gravity-and-beyond, which draws on black holes, field theory and cosmology. Observations and experiments are not a separate domain: every experiment or observation lives with the theory it tests (Michelson-Morley in special-relativity, Eötvös and Pound-Rebka in equivalence-principle, perihelion, deflection, Shapiro delay, gyroscopes and PPN in orbits-light-and-tests, EHT images in black-holes, binary-pulsar decay and LIGO-Virgo events in gravitational-wave-astronomy, supernovae and the CMB in physical-cosmology), so the tutor always retrieves evidence next to the idea it supports. Assignment rules used throughout: a concept belongs to the domain where its general form is taught; a worked instance or named-spacetime version goes to the domain of that spacetime only when it carries physics there; Newtonian constructions that exist only as a foil for one relativistic topic live with that topic; and clusters that are book logistics rather than teachable concepts go to the pseudo-domain discard.

domains.title: Mathematical methods
domains.scope: General-purpose mathematics a learner needs before or alongside the course, taught without reference to spacetime: linear algebra, single- and multivariable calculus, three-dimensional vector calculus, ordinary and partial differential equations, special functions and distributions, Fourier analysis, elementary group theory, and probability and statistics.
excludes: Point-set topology and maps used to define manifolds (open set, homeomorphism, Hausdorff, compactness) belong to manifolds-and-metrics.
Calculus of variations and the Euler-Lagrange equation for particles belong to mechanics-and-newtonian-gravity; for fields, to action-principles-and-field-theory.
Curves and surfaces in Euclidean space (curvature of a curve, Frenet-Serret, Gaussian curvature) belong to curvature.
Bases, components and index notation for spacetime vectors belong to tensor-algebra; abstract vector-space facts stay here.
Statistics applied to gravitational-wave data (matched filtering, false-alarm rate, template banks) belongs to gravitational-wave-astronomy.
Poisson's equation as the law of Newtonian gravity belongs to mechanics-and-newtonian-gravity; the PDE classification and Green-function solution methods stay here.
Cauchy-Kovalevskaya and well-posedness of the Einstein equations belong to einstein-field-equations.

domains.title: Measurement, classical mechanics and Newtonian gravity
domains.scope: Pre-relativistic mechanics and gravity: measurement and unit systems (including the c = 1 and G = c = 1 conventions and dimensional conversion), Newton's laws, inertial frames and fictitious forces, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics of particles, central-force and Kepler orbits, and Newtonian gravity as a field (potential, Poisson and Gauss laws, tides, escape velocity).
excludes: Relativistic orbit equations, the relativistic Binet equation and Schwarzschild effective potentials belong to orbits-light-and-tests.
Equality of inertial and gravitational mass as a principle of gravitation (and the Eötvös-type tests of it) belongs to equivalence-principle; the Newtonian definitions of the masses stay here.

Newtonian constructions used only as a foil inside a relativistic topic go with that topic: Newtonian cosmology and the Newtonian Friedmann derivation to cosmological-dynamics, the Newtonian dark star to black-holes, corpuscular light deflection to orbits-light-and-tests.
Newtonian fluid mechanics and hydrostatics belong to matter-and-stress-energy.
Planck units and the Planck scale belong to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.
Geodesic Lagrangians (the K-Lagrangian, Lagrangian for a relativistic free particle) belong to geodesics-and-symmetries.

domains.title: Electromagnetism, thermal physics and quantum background
domains.scope: Non-gravitational physics background that the three books assume and occasionally re-teach: three-vector electromagnetism (Maxwell equations, potentials and gauge, electromagnetic waves and radiation, energy flux), thermodynamics and statistical mechanics (laws of thermodynamics, black-body radiation, degenerate gases), and the elementary quantum and particle physics needed later (photons, uncertainty, spin, the Standard Model as vocabulary).
excludes: The covariant formulation of electromagnetism (Faraday tensor, four-current, four-potential, Maxwell stress-energy tensor, Maxwell equations in curved spacetime, Einstein-Maxwell equations as a source) belongs to matter-and-stress-energy.

Maxwell's equations in differential-form language and the Hodge dual belong to differential-forms-and-frames; electromagnetism as a gauge field or bundle connection belongs to action-principles-and-field-theory.
Degeneracy pressure, Chandrasekhar mass and neutron-star equations of state applied to stars belong to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars.

Thermodynamics of relativistic fluids (relativistic first law, specific enthalpy in a fluid element) belongs to matter-and-stress-energy; black-hole thermodynamics belongs to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.
Thermal history of the universe, recombination and nucleosynthesis belong to physical-cosmology.
Photon four-momentum and relativistic Doppler shifts belong to special-relativity.

domains.title: Special relativity: kinematics and particle dynamics
domains.scope: Flat spacetime physics without tensors beyond four-vectors: the postulates and their experiments, events and spacetime diagrams, radar and k-calculus, simultaneity, the Lorentz transformation and rapidity, the invariant interval, time dilation and length contraction with their paradoxes, causal classification in Minkowski spacetime, uniformly accelerated observers and Rindler horizons, and relativistic particle mechanics (four-velocity, four-momentum, energy, collisions, photons, Doppler and aberration, observer-measured energy).
includes: invariance of the speed of light
excludes: The algebra of four-vectors as geometric objects (bases, components, dual basis, index notation, scalar product as a metric, transformation matrices) belongs to tensor-algebra; the physical four-vectors and their conservation laws stay here.
Number-flux vectors, dust, perfect fluids and stress-energy tensors in flat spacetime belong to matter-and-stress-energy.
Rindler observers used as the local model of a horizon (near-horizon Rindler approximation, Rindler-Kruskal analogy) belong to black-holes; the Unruh effect belongs to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.
Spacetime as a Lorentzian manifold and Minkowski space in curvilinear coordinates belong to manifolds-and-metrics and connection-and-parallel-transport respectively.
Causal structure of general curved spacetimes (causal future sets, time orientability, conformal diagrams of Minkowski space) belongs to causal-structure-and-singularities.
Relativistic corrections in GPS belong to equivalence-principle.

domains.title: Vectors, one-forms and tensor algebra
domains.scope: Multilinear algebra at a point and calculus in inertial (constant-basis) coordinates: vectors versus their components, bases and dual bases, one-forms as stacks of surfaces, tensors as multilinear slot machines, type/valence, transformation laws, the metric as a vector-to-one-form map, index notation and gymnastics, symmetrization, contraction, the Levi-Civita symbol, and gradients and partial derivatives of tensor fields in Minkowski coordinates.
includes: one-form as a stack of surfaces
metric as a map from vectors to one-forms
valid tensor equation versus component relation
excludes: Anything involving position-dependent bases, including curvilinear coordinates in flat space, Christoffel symbols and covariant derivatives, belongs to connection-and-parallel-transport.
Tangent vectors as derivative operators, tangent and cotangent spaces on manifolds, and tensor densities with their weights belong to manifolds-and-metrics.
Wedge products, p-forms, exterior derivatives and orthonormal frames (vielbeins, tetrads) belong to differential-forms-and-frames.
Abstract vector spaces, matrices and determinants without spacetime content belong to mathematical-methods.
Physical four-vectors (four-velocity, four-momentum) belong to special-relativity.

domains.title: Matter, fields and the stress-energy tensor
domains.scope: How matter and non-gravitational fields are described in relativity and why they gravitate: number flux and conservation of particle number, dust and perfect fluids, the stress-energy tensor as a flux table and its symmetry, local energy-momentum conservation (flat and curved), relativistic fluid dynamics and thermodynamics, Newtonian fluid mechanics as the limit, covariant electromagnetism and the Maxwell stress-energy tensor, scalar-field and vacuum stress-energy, and energy conditions.
includes: projection tensor orthogonal to the four-velocity
energy-momentum tensor of a scalar field
excludes: The variational (Hilbert) definition of the stress-energy tensor and matter Lagrangians belong to action-principles-and-field-theory.
Pressure as a source of gravity in the field equations, the trace of T in trace-reversed equations, and non-localizability of gravitational energy belong to einstein-field-equations.

Fluid equations of state specific to stars (polytropes, degenerate matter, TOV) belong to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars; the cosmic fluid, dilution laws and the fluid equation in an expanding universe belong to cosmological-dynamics.
The effective stress-energy of gravitational waves (Isaacson tensor) belongs to gravitational-waves.
Maxwell equations written with forms belong to differential-forms-and-frames; three-vector Maxwell theory belongs to electromagnetism-thermal-quantum.
Use of energy conditions inside singularity and focusing theorems belongs to causal-structure-and-singularities; the conditions themselves are defined here.

domains.title: Equivalence principle and the principles of general relativity
domains.scope: The physical argument that gravity is geometry and the principles that turn that argument into a theory: universality of free fall and its tests, weak, Einstein and strong equivalence principles, freely falling and local inertial frames as physics, tides as the only local signature of gravity, gravitational redshift and clock effects with their experiments, Mach's principle, general covariance, minimal coupling and the comma-to-semicolon rule, the Newtonian limit of motion and the weak-field metric, and why scalar or flat-space theories of gravity fail.
includes: tidal effects as the signature of gravitation
Newtonian limit of the geodesic equation
gravity as the obstacle to global inertial frames
excludes: The local-flatness theorem and Riemann normal coordinates as mathematics belong to manifolds-and-metrics; the physical use of local inertial frames stays here.
The geodesic equation, affine parameters and conserved quantities along geodesics belong to geodesics-and-symmetries.
Geodesic deviation and the Riemann tensor as tidal tensor belong to curvature.
Redshift at a stellar surface belongs to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars; near a horizon to black-holes; cosmological redshift to cosmological-kinematics.
Solar-system tests other than clock/redshift experiments (perihelion, deflection, Shapiro delay, gyroscopes, PPN) belong to orbits-light-and-tests.
Modern alternative theories of gravity (Brans-Dicke, torsion theories, higher-curvature actions) belong to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.
Linearized metric perturbations with gauge freedom belong to gravitational-waves; the Newtonian limit of the field equations (fixing 8 pi G) belongs to einstein-field-equations.
The hole argument belongs to einstein-field-equations.

domains.title: Manifolds, metrics and integration
domains.scope: Spacetime as a differentiable manifold equipped with a metric: topological prerequisites, charts, atlases and transition maps, maps between manifolds (push-forward, pull-back, diffeomorphisms), tangent vectors as derivations, tangent and cotangent spaces and vector fields, the metric tensor field, line elements, signature and reading a metric, light cones drawn from a metric, embeddings and induced metrics, conformally related metrics, the local-flatness theorem, tensor densities, volume elements and integration, and Gauss's theorem on a manifold.
includes: square root of minus the metric determinant
excludes: Lie derivatives, Lie brackets, Killing vectors and isometries belong to geodesics-and-symmetries.
Covariant derivatives, connection coefficients and parallel transport belong to connection-and-parallel-transport.
Intrinsic and extrinsic curvature of surfaces and the curvature of embedded 2-surfaces belong to curvature.
Volume forms, integration of p-forms and the generalized Stokes theorem belong to differential-forms-and-frames; densities and coordinate volume elements stay here.
Fibre bundles, base spaces and fibres belong to action-principles-and-field-theory.
Hypersurface foliations with lapse, shift and extrinsic curvature as evolution variables belong to einstein-field-equations; the induced metric of a submanifold stays here.

Embedding diagrams of specific spacetimes go with those spacetimes (Flamm paraboloid to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars, wormhole throats to black-holes, de Sitter hyperboloids to cosmological-dynamics).
Global causal properties, time orientation and conformal compactification belong to causal-structure-and-singularities.

domains.title: Connection, covariant derivative and parallel transport
domains.scope: Differentiating tensors when bases change from point to point: curvilinear coordinates in flat space as the rehearsal, Christoffel symbols and their non-tensorial transformation, the covariant derivative of vectors, one-forms and general tensors, the affine connection and its axioms, metric compatibility and torsion-freeness (the Levi-Civita connection and its uniqueness), Christoffel symbols from the metric, the absolute derivative along a curve, parallel transport of vectors, and Fermi transport.
includes: Christoffel symbols of plane polar coordinates
Leibniz rule for the covariant derivative
non-zero connection coefficients do not imply curvature
excludes: The geodesic equation, geodesics as autoparallels, affine parameters and variational methods for geodesics belong to geodesics-and-symmetries (reading Christoffel symbols off a geodesic Lagrangian included).
Path dependence of parallel transport, holonomy around loops and the Riemann tensor as the commutator of covariant derivatives belong to curvature.
Connection one-forms and the Cartan structure equations belong to differential-forms-and-frames.
Gauge covariant derivatives and bundle connections belong to action-principles-and-field-theory.
Christoffel symbols of a named spacetime computed as a worked example go with that spacetime's domain only when they are used as physics there; the computational technique stays here.
The comma-to-semicolon rule as a physical principle belongs to equivalence-principle.

domains.title: Geodesics, symmetries and conserved quantities
domains.scope: Curves of free fall and the symmetries that make them solvable: the geodesic equation and geodesics as autoparallel and extremal curves, affine and non-affine parametrization, timelike, null and spacelike geodesics, variational derivations (arc-length and K-Lagrangians), maximal proper time, conjugate points, geodesic postulate; Lie dragging, Lie derivatives and brackets, Killing's equation, Killing vectors and isometry groups, stationary, static and axisymmetric spacetimes, and conserved energy and angular momentum along geodesics from metric symmetries.
includes: maximal proper time of timelike geodesics
great circles as geodesics of the sphere
geodesic equation with an external force
conserved quantity along a geodesic from a Killing vector
excludes: Parallel transport of arbitrary vectors and the covariant derivative itself belong to connection-and-parallel-transport.

Geodesic deviation and tidal acceleration belong to curvature; geodesic congruences, expansion/shear/rotation, Raychaudhuri focusing and conjugate-point theorems used for singularities belong to causal-structure-and-singularities.

Motion in specific spacetimes goes with them: Schwarzschild orbits and photon trajectories to orbits-light-and-tests, Kerr orbits and the Carter constant to black-holes, cosmological geodesics and peculiar-momentum decay to cosmological-kinematics.
The Newtonian limit of geodesic motion belongs to equivalence-principle.
Noether's theorem for fields and diffeomorphism invariance as the origin of conservation laws belong to action-principles-and-field-theory; the Killing-vector recipe for particles stays here.
Komar mass and other global charges built from Killing vectors belong to einstein-field-equations.

domains.title: Curvature
domains.scope: Measuring how a geometry fails to be flat: curvature of curves and surfaces in Euclidean space (Gaussian curvature, theorema egregium, extrinsic versus intrinsic), path dependence and holonomy of parallel transport, the Riemann tensor from loops and commutators with its symmetries, component counting and identities (cyclic, Bianchi), Ricci tensor and scalar, Einstein tensor as geometry, Weyl tensor and conformal flatness, sectional curvature, curvature invariants, geodesic deviation and the relativistic tidal tensor, and spaces of constant curvature (sphere, hyperbolic plane).
includes: holonomy of parallel transport around a closed loop
angle excess of a geodesic triangle
excludes: Curvature 2-forms, Cartan's method for computing curvature and the Cartan form of the Bianchi identity belong to differential-forms-and-frames.
The Einstein tensor as the left side of the field equations, uniqueness arguments (Lovelock) and vacuum Ricci-flatness as a field equation belong to einstein-field-equations.

Curvature of a named spacetime goes with it when it carries physics there: Schwarzschild tidal tensor and Kretschmann scalar to black-holes, Robertson-Walker Ricci components to cosmological-kinematics, linearized Riemann tensor to gravitational-waves.
Gauss-Codazzi and Ricci equations for spacelike slices of spacetime belong to einstein-field-equations; the classical Gauss-Codazzi equations for surfaces in three-space stay here.
Petrov classification, principal null directions and the Newman-Penrose description of the Weyl tensor belong to gravitational-waves.
Raychaudhuri's equation and focusing belong to causal-structure-and-singularities.
De Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes as solutions belong to cosmological-dynamics; constant-curvature Riemann tensors in general stay here.

domains.title: Differential forms, orthonormal frames and Cartan methods
domains.scope: Index-free exterior calculus and frame methods: wedge product and p-forms with their geometric pictures, p-vectors and pairings, exterior derivative and dd = 0, closed and exact forms and the Poincaré lemma, integration of forms, chains and boundaries, the generalized Stokes theorem, volume forms and the Hodge star, orthonormal frames, vielbeins and tetrads (including null tetrads), frame components as what observers measure, connection 1-forms, Cartan's structure equations and curvature 2-forms, and Maxwell's equations in form language.
includes: boundary of a boundary is zero
orthonormal frame of a static observer
Maxwell equations in differential form language
excludes: Ordinary tensor algebra, the Levi-Civita symbol in index form and symmetrization brackets belong to tensor-algebra.
Lie derivatives (including Cartan's formula relating them to d) belong to geodesics-and-symmetries.
Coordinate volume elements and tensor densities belong to manifolds-and-metrics.
Gauge fields as bundle connections, the gauge-gravity dictionary and Kaluza-Klein reduction belong to action-principles-and-field-theory and quantum-gravity-and-beyond respectively.
Newman-Penrose spin coefficients, Petrov types and optical scalars used for radiation belong to gravitational-waves; the null tetrad as a frame stays here.
Frames adapted to specific spacetimes go with those spacetimes only when they carry physics there (ZAMO frames to black-holes); the static-observer frame technique stays here.
Three-vector Maxwell theory belongs to electromagnetism-thermal-quantum; covariant tensor Maxwell theory to matter-and-stress-energy.

domains.title: Einstein field equations and their structure
domains.scope: Getting and understanding the field equations: heuristic routes (Poisson plus covariance plus conservation, tidal analogy), the Einstein equation with and without a cosmological constant, vacuum equations, trace reversal, fixing the coupling from the Newtonian limit, pressure as a source, nonlinearity, counting degrees of freedom and gauge, equations of motion from conservation, the hole argument, mass and energy in GR (far-field, ADM and Komar mass, non-localizability of gravitational energy, positive energy theorem), and the initial-value formulation: constraints, Cauchy problem, 3+1 and 2+2 splits, lapse and shift, extrinsic curvature of slices, Gauss-Codazzi-Ricci equations, gauge conditions, hyperbolicity and numerical relativity.
includes: Einstein field equation with cosmological constant
Newtonian limit of the field equation
pressure as a source of gravity
degrees of freedom of the metric
equation of motion from the field equation
total mass of a stationary relativistic body
excludes: Deriving the field equations from an action (Einstein-Hilbert, Palatini, boundary terms) belongs to action-principles-and-field-theory.
Linearized field equations, the Lorenz/harmonic gauge in perturbation theory and weak-field gauge freedom belong to gravitational-waves.
The geometric definitions of the Einstein tensor and Bianchi identities belong to curvature.

The cosmological constant as dark energy or vacuum energy in cosmology belongs to cosmological-dynamics and physical-cosmology; the vacuum-energy (cosmological constant) problem belongs to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.
Bondi mass, news functions and mass loss by radiation belong to gravitational-waves.
Cauchy surfaces, domains of dependence and global hyperbolicity as causal notions belong to causal-structure-and-singularities; their role in the initial-value problem is referenced, not duplicated.

Specific exact solutions go to their domains (Schwarzschild to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars, Kerr and Reissner-Nordström to black-holes, Friedmann models to cosmological-dynamics, exact waves to gravitational-waves).

domains.title: Action principles, classical field theory and gauge fields
domains.scope: General relativity as a Lagrangian field theory: actions and Lagrangian densities, Euler-Lagrange equations for fields, functional derivatives and metric variations, the Einstein-Hilbert action and its variation (Palatini identity, boundary terms), matter actions and the Hilbert stress-energy tensor, diffeomorphism invariance and Noether's theorem, scalar and Maxwell field theories, spontaneous symmetry breaking, and gauge theory with fibre bundles as the geometric language shared by electromagnetism and gravity.
includes: variation with respect to the metric
boundary term in the Einstein-Hilbert variation
excludes: Particle Lagrangians and the calculus of variations for finite-dimensional systems belong to mechanics-and-newtonian-gravity; geodesic Lagrangians belong to geodesics-and-symmetries.
Stress-energy tensors of matter models written down directly (dust, fluids, Maxwell, scalar field) belong to matter-and-stress-energy; only the variational definition lives here.
Quantization of fields, gravitons, Kaluza-Klein theory, effective field theory of gravity, string actions and higher-curvature corrections belong to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.
The inflaton and slow-roll dynamics belong to physical-cosmology.
Quadratic Lagrangians for linearized gravity belong to gravitational-waves.
Hamiltonian (ADM) canonical variables of general relativity belong to einstein-field-equations.

domains.title: Spherical symmetry: Schwarzschild geometry and relativistic stars
domains.scope: Static spherically symmetric spacetimes outside and inside matter: the general static spherical metric and areal radius, deriving the Schwarzschild exterior, Birkhoff's theorem, what Schwarzschild coordinates and mass mean operationally (proper radial distance, static observers, Flamm embedding, isotropic coordinates), surface redshift, the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation and mass function, interior solutions and matching, the Buchdahl bound, and compact-star astrophysics (white dwarfs, neutron stars, Chandrasekhar limit, supernovae, pulsars).
includes: neutron star equation of state and maximum mass
excludes: Test-particle and photon motion in the Schwarzschild exterior (effective potentials, ISCO, photon sphere, perihelion shift, light bending) belongs to orbits-light-and-tests.
The horizon at r = 2M, its coordinate extensions, collapse to a black hole and the r = 0 singularity belong to black-holes.
Gravitational waves from neutron stars (continuous waves, tidal deformability, kilonovae, mergers) belong to gravitational-wave-astronomy.
Degenerate Fermi gases as statistical physics belong to electromagnetism-thermal-quantum.
Einstein-tensor computations for a general spherical metric are shared with cosmology but live here.
Reissner-Nordström and Kerr metrics belong to black-holes.

domains.title: Orbits, light propagation and tests of general relativity
domains.scope: Motion of test bodies and light in weak fields and in the Schwarzschild exterior, and the experiments and observations that test these predictions: effective potentials for particles and photons, circular, bound, plunging and scattering orbits, ISCO and photon sphere, relativistic perihelion precession, light deflection and gravitational lensing, Shapiro delay, gyroscope (geodetic and frame-dragging) precession tests, the parametrized post-Newtonian framework, and binary-pulsar periastron advance.
includes: orbital period of a circular Schwarzschild orbit
excludes: Gravitational redshift and clock experiments belong to equivalence-principle.
General machinery for conserved quantities from Killing vectors belongs to geodesics-and-symmetries; its application to Schwarzschild orbits lives here.
Orbits inside the horizon, radial infall across r = 2M, black-hole shadows, and all Kerr orbits (Carter constant, prograde/retrograde ISCO) belong to black-holes.
Orbital decay of binary pulsars by gravitational radiation and gravitational-wave tests of GR belong to gravitational-wave-astronomy.
Newtonian Kepler orbits belong to mechanics-and-newtonian-gravity; the Newtonian corpuscular deflection used as a foil lives here.
Frame dragging as a linearized-gravity effect (gravitomagnetism, Lense-Thirring field) belongs to gravitational-waves; its experimental tests live here.
Lensing used as a cosmological probe (weak lensing surveys of dark matter) belongs to physical-cosmology; lensing optics lives here.
Alternative theories themselves belong to quantum-gravity-and-beyond; the PPN framework for comparing them lives here.

domains.title: Black holes
domains.scope: Classical black holes from horizon to astrophysics: the nature of r = 2M, coordinate versus curvature singularity in Schwarzschild, tortoise, Eddington-Finkelstein, Painlevé-Gullstrand and Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates, the maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime with its Penrose diagram, white holes and Einstein-Rosen bridges, radial infall and tidal disruption, gravitational collapse, event horizons, Reissner-Nordström and Kerr(-Newman) black holes with inner horizons, ergosphere, frame dragging, Penrose process and Kerr orbits, uniqueness and no-hair results, the area theorem, and astrophysical black holes and their observation.
includes: Penrose diagram of the Kruskal spacetime
gravitational collapse to a black hole
excludes: The Schwarzschild exterior solution, Birkhoff's theorem and static-observer physics outside r = 2M belong to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars; orbits and photon spheres outside the horizon belong to orbits-light-and-tests.
Hawking radiation, black-hole temperature and entropy, laws of black-hole mechanics, evaporation, the information problem and the Unruh effect belong to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

General causal-structure tools (conformal compactification technique, trapped surfaces in general, singularity theorems, cosmic censorship, Raychaudhuri focusing) belong to causal-structure-and-singularities; their application to a named black hole lives here.
Black-hole mergers, ringdown, quasinormal modes as observed signals and black-hole populations from gravitational-wave catalogs belong to gravitational-wave-astronomy.
Wormholes requiring exotic matter (traversable wormholes) belong to causal-structure-and-singularities.

domains.title: Causal structure, asymptotics and singularities
domains.scope: Global methods for arbitrary spacetimes: causal curves and causal future and past, time orientability, closed timelike curves and causality conditions, Cauchy surfaces, domains of dependence and global hyperbolicity, conformal compactification and Penrose diagrams as a technique (Minkowski as the model), null and timelike infinity and asymptotic flatness, horizons as causal boundaries in general, geodesic congruences with expansion, shear and rotation, the Raychaudhuri equation and focusing, trapped surfaces, singularities as geodesic incompleteness and their classification, singularity theorems, cosmic censorship, and spacetime topology.
excludes: Causal classification of vectors and the light cone in Minkowski spacetime belong to special-relativity.

Penrose diagrams of specific spacetimes go with those spacetimes: Kruskal, Reissner-Nordström and Kerr to black-holes, Robertson-Walker and de Sitter to cosmological-kinematics and cosmological-dynamics.
Event horizons of named black holes and the coordinate singularity at r = 2M belong to black-holes.
Energy conditions are defined in matter-and-stress-energy and used here.
The Cauchy problem, constraints and 3+1 evolution belong to einstein-field-equations.
Asymptotic mass definitions (ADM, Komar) belong to einstein-field-equations; Bondi mass, peeling and the BMS group belong to gravitational-waves.
Particle and event horizons in cosmology belong to cosmological-kinematics; the horizon problem to physical-cosmology.

domains.title: Linearized gravity and gravitational-wave theory
domains.scope: Gravity as a small perturbation and the waves it supports, as theory: metric perturbations on flat space, gauge transformations and the Lorenz (harmonic) gauge, trace reversal and the linearized field equations, gravitomagnetism and the Lense-Thirring field, plane-wave solutions and the transverse-traceless gauge, polarizations and their effect on test masses, wave energy and the Isaacson tensor, generation by the quadrupole formula and radiation reaction, binary inspiral theory and chirp mass, the absence of monopole and dipole radiation, exact plane and colliding waves, Bondi radiating spacetimes, news and peeling, and Petrov classification.
includes: gauge transformation of the metric perturbation
geodesic deviation in a gravitational wave
effective energy-momentum tensor of gravitational waves
energy flux of a gravitational wave
absence of monopole and dipole gravitational radiation
binary inspiral driven by gravitational radiation
retarded solution of the linearized field equation
excludes: The Newtonian-limit weak-field metric and gravitational redshift belong to equivalence-principle.

Detectors and their response (interferometers, resonant bars, radar return time, antenna patterns, detector tensor), noise, data analysis, astrophysical sources, specific detections, standard sirens and GW tests of GR belong to gravitational-wave-astronomy.
Tests of frame dragging (Gravity Probe B, LAGEOS) belong to orbits-light-and-tests.
Gravitons, spin-2 field quantization and graviton exchange belong to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.
Primordial gravitational waves from inflation and CMB B-modes belong to physical-cosmology.
Quasinormal modes as black-hole perturbation theory are taught here; ringdown as an observed signal belongs to gravitational-wave-astronomy.

domains.title: Gravitational-wave detection and astronomy
domains.scope: Gravitational waves as an observational science: how detectors respond (interferometer arm-length changes, return-time response, resonant bars, detector tensor and antenna patterns), detector technology and noise sources, signal analysis (matched filtering, template banks, signal-to-noise, false alarms, coincidence and coherent networks, null streams, sky localization), source classes and their scaling laws (compact binaries, continuous waves, bursts, stochastic backgrounds), specific detections and catalogs, binary-pulsar orbital decay, pulsar timing arrays and space missions, multimessenger astronomy, standard sirens, and tests of general relativity with waves.
includes: return time response of a beam detector
amplitude spectral density of detector noise
continuous gravitational waves from spinning neutron stars
gravitational wave test of general relativity
excludes: Wave solutions, polarizations, TT gauge, energy flux, the quadrupole formula and chirp-mass derivation belong to gravitational-waves.
Binary-pulsar periastron advance and other orbital-dynamics tests belong to orbits-light-and-tests.
Neutron-star and black-hole physics apart from their gravitational-wave signatures belongs to schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars and black-holes.
The Hubble constant from sirens is measured here; its cosmological interpretation and the Hubble tension belong to physical-cosmology.
Generic statistics (Bayes' theorem, likelihoods, Gaussian noise as a random process) belongs to mathematical-methods.
Primordial backgrounds from inflation as cosmology belong to physical-cosmology; searches for backgrounds live here.

domains.title: Cosmology I: geometry and kinematics of an expanding universe
domains.scope: The geometry of a homogeneous, isotropic universe and what observers measure in it, independent of which matter drives the expansion: cosmological and Copernican principles, Weyl's postulate, comoving observers and cosmic time, the Robertson-Walker metric and its three spatial geometries, the scale factor and Hubble parameter, Hubble-Lemaître law, cosmological redshift, peculiar motion, distance measures (proper, comoving, luminosity, angular-diameter) and lookback time, conformal time, particle and event horizons, and Penrose diagrams of Robertson-Walker models.
includes: decay of peculiar momentum with expansion
proper distance in a Robertson-Walker spacetime
Penrose diagram of a Robertson-Walker model
Ricci tensor of the Robertson-Walker metric
excludes: Friedmann and acceleration equations, density parameters, dilution laws, model universes, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter solutions, the age of the universe and fate of the universe belong to cosmological-dynamics.
Measured values and data (distance ladder, Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram, CMB, H0 tension) belong to physical-cosmology.
Constant-curvature geometry in general belongs to curvature; its cosmological use lives here.
The horizon problem and its inflationary solution belong to physical-cosmology; the horizon definitions live here.
General conformal-compactification technique belongs to causal-structure-and-singularities.

domains.title: Cosmology II: Friedmann dynamics and model universes
domains.scope: How the field equations drive the scale factor: Newtonian cosmology as a warm-up, the Friedmann and acceleration equations, the fluid equation and dilution of matter, radiation and vacuum energy, critical density and density parameters, the cosmological constant in cosmology and vacuum energy as a perfect fluid, the effective-potential and phase-plane analysis of the expansion, the catalogue of model universes (Einstein static, Einstein-de Sitter, Milne, de Sitter, anti-de Sitter, Lemaître, Eddington-Lemaître, closed and open dust, bouncing and loitering), the big bang and big crunch singularities in these models, age estimates, and the steady-state alternative.
includes: scaling of energy density with the scale factor
vacuum energy as a perfect fluid
effective potential for the scale factor
instability of the Einstein static universe
excludes: The metric, redshift, distances and horizons of Robertson-Walker spacetimes belong to cosmological-kinematics.
The observational determination of parameters, Lambda-CDM as a concordance model, dark matter and dark energy evidence, thermal history, CMB and inflation belong to physical-cosmology.
The cosmological constant as a term in the field equations belongs to einstein-field-equations; the vacuum-energy (cosmological constant) problem belongs to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

General singularity theorems (including the cosmological singularity theorem) and BKL/Kasner behaviour belong to causal-structure-and-singularities; the explicit a = 0 singularity of Friedmann models lives here.
Anti-de Sitter space in holography (AdS/CFT, conformal boundary as a duality arena) belongs to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

domains.title: Cosmology III: physical and observational cosmology
domains.scope: The real universe and the evidence for its history: the cosmic distance ladder and Type Ia supernovae, the measured Hubble constant and tension, accelerating expansion and dark energy, dark matter evidence and candidates, the hot big bang and thermal history, big bang nucleosynthesis, recombination and the cosmic microwave background with its anisotropies and polarization, baryon acoustic oscillations, structure formation and density perturbations, Lambda-CDM as the standard model, and inflation (horizon and flatness problems, inflaton and slow roll, reheating, primordial perturbations and gravitational waves).
includes: CMB anisotropy and angular power spectrum
excludes: Definitions of redshift, distances and horizons belong to cosmological-kinematics; the Friedmann equations and model catalogue belong to cosmological-dynamics.
Detecting stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds and standard-siren H0 measurements belong to gravitational-wave-astronomy.
Quantum cosmology, the cosmological constant problem, anthropic arguments and multiverse ideas belong to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.
Scalar field theory and spontaneous symmetry breaking in general belong to action-principles-and-field-theory; their early-universe application lives here.
Black-body radiation as thermal physics belongs to electromagnetism-thermal-quantum.

domains.title: Quantum effects, quantum gravity and beyond Einstein
domains.scope: Where general relativity meets quantum physics and where it may be modified: quantum fields in curved spacetime and the Unruh effect, Hawking radiation, black-hole temperature, entropy and the laws of black-hole mechanics, evaporation and the information problem, gravitons and gravity as a spin-2 field, effective field theory of gravity and non-renormalizability, Planck units, Kaluza-Klein theory and extra dimensions, string theory, loop quantum gravity, holography and AdS/CFT, the cosmological constant problem, quantum cosmology, and modern alternative classical theories of gravity.
includes: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
negative heat capacity of black holes
spin of the mediator and sign of the force
higher curvature corrections to the Einstein-Hilbert action
excludes: The classical area theorem, no-hair and uniqueness theorems belong to black-holes.
Classical field theory, gauge fields and bundles belong to action-principles-and-field-theory.
Using the PPN framework to test alternative theories belongs to orbits-light-and-tests; historical scalar theories used to motivate geometric gravity belong to equivalence-principle.
Inflation and primordial perturbations as cosmology belong to physical-cosmology.
Elementary quantum mechanics (uncertainty, photons, spin) belongs to electromagnetism-thermal-quantum.
